newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500 futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500 futures end sharply lower.

text.p: June Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended sharply lower in fast-market trading, slumping to the lowest price in three months.
Traders said the market decisively rejected Tuesday's rally and the midday attempt today to cut losses.

"We're going to see a lot of volatility," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "Overall, people want to see this thing correct 10 percent," he added, saying bearish traders hold targets at 6,400 in the Dow and 745.00 in S&P 500s.
Other traders said rate hike fears swirled through the market and said players were nervous before Friday's data.
Volume was heavy and Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed an estimated June S&P 500 volume of 97,000 contracts.
"It felt like it was a fast market all day," one trader said. Another trader called price action erratic.
"We have wide spreads between bid and offer and gobs of trading, but the trade is erratic," he said.

"They're bouncing around as opposed to more orderly moves," he said. "The market is trying to deal with the reality of more than 25 basis points," he said, referring to the notion that more Fed rate hikes are at hand.

A Washington Post story got the ball rolling this morning, with traders taking comments from Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer to mean a forward-looking Fed will raise interest rates again. He said the U.S. economy was "really strong" and "not a fluke."

"Maybe two more 25 basis point hikes isn't going to be all that's in the cards," one futures trader said. "I think we've been pricing in another two hikes and now we're pricing in another one or two more after that."
The Fed raised the fed funds target 25 basis points in its March policy meeting, and will meet again May 20.
Traders noted worries ahead of Friday's key employment data. A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast for a 182,000 jobs gain in March, compared with 339,000 in February.

At the close, June S&P 500s were down 13.70 points at 751.30, Midcap 400s were down 1.65 pts at 250.50, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 240.0 to 18,080.0, Nasdaq 100s fell 19.10 pts to 787.25 and KCBT Value Line futures fell 8.50 to 679.50.
